...but his self-ownership is a cosmic concept. Higher beings on some higher plane are doing godly things and they stop, look down, and say to each other: "hmm... that little human thing owns his own life. We can fuck right off then, guys. Let's go."

Ownership itself is only a concept. I'm not sure how it's a "cosmic" concept, "cosmic" being a word I attach to concepts which are ill or vaguely defined. But we were talking about the original statement about the presumption of assigning "purpose" to a cogs-and-wheels universe. Unless these higher beings created earthly life for some concrete "purpose" only they know, the universe is just as purposeless for them, as it is for us.

Thinking that there has to be a purpose or meaning to life is running away from your problem. No one is going to hand you anything out of their own free will, least of all the universe or whatever supreme being created it. All that anyone and anything on this planet is, is just a gigantic collection of vibrating strings moving together and shooting particles at each other, and any attempt to think otherwise is foolishness.

I always thought it sounded like kind of a meaningless question. Because for something to have a purpose begs the question, "Whose purpose?" A chair may have one purpose for me, and another for a "professional" wrestler. A dirty old shoe may have one purpose for me, and another for a dog. So, when you're asking what purpose life has, do you mean your own life, or life in general? When you say "My life has purpose X," it is understood that you mean "purpose X to me." Because your life may have a very different purpose to somebody else. But when you ask what the purpose of life in general is in some "greater," nebulous sense - a sense not related to Darwinian evolution - you can never get an answer out of anybody that is more coherent than "To glorify God." Some people will say things like, "To be happy," or "To be the best you can be." But, says who? Them? How did they get the right to categorically decide the purpose of life and everybody living it?
